item_name: Staff Assessment of Resident Mood (PHQ-9-OV©) — E. Poor appetite or overeating

lookback_source.quote: Conduct the interviews during the 7-day look-back period based on the ARD.

lookback_notes: The assessor's observation/administration window is the 7-day look-back period based on the ARD (p. D-13). A separate symptom-recall period is embedded in the staff questions themselves: "Over the last 2 weeks, did the resident have any of the following problems or behaviors?" (p. D-12) and "Ask the staff member being interviewed to select how often over the past 2 weeks the symptom occurred" (p. D-15). The coexistence of the two windows is recorded in conflicts.

coding_levels.label: No (Column 1, Symptom Presence)
coding_levels.definition: Code 0, no: if symptoms listed are not present. Enter 0 in Column 2, Symptom Frequency.

source.quote: Code 0, no: if symptoms listed are not present. Enter 0 in Column 2, Symptom Frequency.

coding_levels.label: Yes (Column 1, Symptom Presence)
coding_levels.definition: Code 1, yes: if symptoms listed are present. Enter 0, 1, 2, or 3 in Column 2, Symptom Frequency.

source.quote: Code 1, yes: if symptoms listed are present. Enter 0, 1, 2, or 3 in Column 2, Symptom Frequency.

coding_levels.label: Never or 1 day (Column 2, Symptom Frequency)
coding_levels.definition: Code 0, never or 1 day: if staff indicate that the resident has never or has experienced the symptom on only 1 day.

source.quote: Code 0, never or 1 day: if staff indicate that the resident has never or has experienced the symptom on only 1 day.

coding_levels.label: 2-6 days (several days) (Column 2, Symptom Frequency)
coding_levels.definition: Code 1, 2-6 days (several days): if staff indicate that the resident has experienced the symptom for 2-6 days.

source.quote: Code 1, 2-6 days (several days): if staff indicate that the resident has experienced the symptom for 2-6 days.

coding_levels.label: 7-11 days (half or more of the days) (Column 2, Symptom Frequency)
coding_levels.definition: Code 2, 7-11 days (half or more of the days): if staff indicate that the resident has experienced the symptom for 7-11 days.

source.quote: Code 2, 7-11 days (half or more of the days): if staff indicate that the resident has experienced the symptom for 7-11 days.

coding_levels.label: 12-14 days (nearly every day) (Column 2, Symptom Frequency)
coding_levels.definition: Code 3, 12-14 days (nearly every day): if staff indicate that the resident has experienced the symptom for 12-14 days.

source.quote: Code 3, 12-14 days (nearly every day): if staff indicate that the resident has experienced the symptom for 12-14 days.

federal_coding_rules.rule: D0500 (including item E, Poor appetite or overeating) is not conducted if the Resident Mood Interview (D0150–D0160) was completed.

source.quote: Do not conduct if Resident Mood Interview (D0150–D0160) was completed

federal_coding_rules.rule: The Staff Assessment of Resident Mood is completed only when D0100 is coded 0, No; it is not completed based on resident performance during the Resident Mood Interview.

source.quote: The assessor will complete the Staff Assessment only when D0100 is coded 0, No. The assessor does not complete the Staff Assessment based on resident performance during the Resident Mood Interview.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Do not complete the Staff Assessment of Resident Mood items (D0500) if the resident interview should have been conducted but was not done, or if the assessment being completed is a stand-alone Part A PPS Discharge assessment.

source.quote: Do not complete the Staff Assessment of Resident Mood items (D0500) if the resident interview should have been conducted but was not done, or if the assessment being completed is a stand-alone Part A PPS Discharge assessment.

federal_coding_rules.rule: If symptom frequency in D0150A2 through D0150I2 is blank or dashed for 3 or more items, the resident interview is deemed not complete, Total Severity Score is coded 99, the Staff Assessment of Mood is not completed, and the assessor skips to D0700.

source.quote: If symptom frequency in items D0150A2 through D0150I2 is blank or dashed for 3 or more items, the interview is deemed NOT complete. Total Severity Score should be coded as "99," do not complete the Staff Assessment of Mood, and skip to D0700, Social Isolation.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Item E is coded in two columns: Column 1 Symptom Presence (enter 1 if symptom present) and then Column 2 Symptom Frequency.

source.quote: If symptom is present, enter 1 (yes) in column 1, Symptom Presence. Then move to column 2, Symptom Frequency, and indicate symptom frequency.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Staff interviews for this item are conducted during the 7-day look-back period based on the ARD.

source.quote: Conduct the interviews during the 7-day look-back period based on the ARD.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Interview staff from all shifts who know the resident best; conduct the staff interview in a location that protects resident privacy.

source.quote: Interview staff from all shifts who know the resident best. Conduct the staff interview in a location that protects resident privacy.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Encourage staff to report symptom frequency even if the staff believes the symptom to be unrelated to depression.

source.quote: Encourage staff to report symptom frequency, even if the staff believes the symptom to be unrelated to depression.

federal_coding_rules.rule: If frequency cannot be determined by staff interview because the resident has been in the facility for less than 2 weeks, talk to family or significant other and review transfer records to inform selection of a frequency code.

source.quote: If frequency cannot be determined by staff interview because the resident has been in the facility for less than 2 weeks, talk to family or significant other and review transfer records to inform the selection of a frequency code.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Ask the staff member to select how often over the past 2 weeks the symptom occurred, using the descriptive and/or numeric categories on the form.

source.quote: Ask the staff member being interviewed to select how often over the past 2 weeks the symptom occurred. Use the descriptive and/or numeric categories on the form (e.g., "nearly every day" or 3 = 12-14 days) to select a frequency response.

federal_coding_rules.rule: If a longer item is separated into its component parts (e.g., "poor appetite" and "overeating"), select the highest frequency rating reported.

source.quote: If you separated a longer item into its component parts, select the highest frequency rating that is reported.

federal_coding_rules.rule: If the staff member has difficulty selecting between two frequency responses, code for the higher frequency.

source.quote: If the staff member has difficulty selecting between two frequency responses, code for the higher frequency.

federal_coding_rules.rule: If the resident has been in the facility for less than 2 weeks, also talk to the family or significant other and review transfer records to inform selection of the frequency code.

source.quote: If the resident has been in the facility for less than 2 weeks, also talk to the family or significant other and review transfer records to inform selection of the frequency code.

federal_coding_rules.rule: The Column 2 frequency score for this item is added with the other D0500 frequency items to produce D0600, Total Severity Score (maximum 30); the D0600 interview is successfully completed if staff answered the frequency responses of at least 8 out of 10 items.

source.quote: The interview is successfully completed if the staff members were able to answer the frequency responses of at least 8 out of 10 items on the PHQ-9-OV©.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Certain staff responses to D0500E (e.g., "They have not wanted to eat much of anything lately"; "They have a voracious appetite, more so than last week") indicate the need for follow-up questioning with the staff member.

source.quote:
D0500E, Poor Appetite or Overeating 
• They have not wanted to eat much of anything lately. 
• They have a voracious appetite, more so than last week.

federal.criterion: When the resident has been in the facility less than 2 weeks and staff cannot determine frequency, information from family or significant other and review of transfer records is used to inform the frequency code.

source.quote: If frequency cannot be determined by staff interview because the resident has been in the facility for less than 2 weeks, talk to family or significant other and review transfer records to inform the selection of a frequency code.

federal.notes: Manual frames this as a required step when the standard staff-interview source is insufficient.

federal.criterion: Coding is based on interviews with staff from all shifts who know the resident best, conducted in a location that protects resident privacy.

source.quote: Interview staff from all shifts who know the resident best. Conduct the staff interview in a location that protects resident privacy.

federal.notes: Stated as Step for Assessment; the pages do not specify any chart documentation requirement.

case_mix_relevance.notes: The supplied Section D pages do not tie D0500E to any payment or case-mix classification.

conflicts.topic: Two coexisting time windows for D0500E: the 7-day assessor look-back period versus the 2-week symptom-recall period asked of staff.

positions.claim: The staff interviews are conducted during the 7-day look-back period based on the ARD.

source.quote: Conduct the interviews during the 7-day look-back period based on the ARD.

positions.claim: The staff assessment question and frequency coding cover the last/past 2 weeks.

source.quote: Over the last 2 weeks, did the resident have any of the following problems or behaviors?

positions.claim: Staff are asked to select how often over the past 2 weeks the symptom occurred.

source.quote: Ask the staff member being interviewed to select how often over the past 2 weeks the symptom occurred.

conflicts.resolution: unresolved — surface to user. The pages state the interview is administered within the 7-day look-back based on the ARD while the symptom frequency asked of staff spans the past 2 weeks; the document does not reconcile the two windows.
